To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tumorigenic activity of substituted organohalide derivatives may be related to the presence of a nucleophilic group and to a molecular conformation which stabilizes the transition of the alkylating species.

the abilities of organohalides, especially those containing nucleophilic substituents, to induce lung tumors correlate with the abilities of these compounds to form carbonium ions and with the general toxicity of these compounds toward strain A male mice.

four organohalides were found to induce lung tumors significantly, that five organohalides showed borderline tumor activity, and that 23 of the 28 organohalogens tested showed no significant tumor response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of pulmonary adenomas by substituted organoholides in strain A mice.
the induction of pulmonary adenomas by a series of substituted organohalide compounds in strain A mice.
identifying the chemical structures of compounds that are carcinogenic in the mouse lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
2-bromo-, 2-chlorobutane, 3-bromo-, and 3-chlropropionic acids are the only compounds in the series studied which are tumorigenic in the lungs of strain A mice.
only four of the 28 organohalo compounds tested were tumorigenic, and that the tumorigenicity was probably due to the presence of a nucleophilic group in the molecule.
9 organohalides of the 28 tested are tumorigenic for the mouse lung, 4 of which are tumorigenic at doses lower than similar unsubstituated compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tumorigenic organohalides are those compounds in which a nucleophilic group is attached to a carbon adjacent to the halogen.

the organochalides tested are tumorigenic only when the molecule contains a nucleophilically activated group, and that the tumorigenicity of such compounds may be due to their biological alkylating activity.
the organohalides tested can be divided into two groups: the tumorigenic compounds and the nontumorigenic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a nucleophilic functional group is required for organohalide tumorigenesis.
the presence of a nucleophilic group on an organohalide can enhance tumorigenic activity, and that this effect may be due to stabilization of the transition state of a biological alkylating species.
organohalides which contain nucleophilic substituents and which have the ability to form stable carbonium ions may be potent pulmonary carcinogens.
